senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; v. שׁוּם a. mark, name, title, nature, denomination.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 3:3">Pes. III, 3</cite> <he>לא תקרא לה שם וכ׳</he> she must not name it (declare it to be Ḥallah) until it is baked.
<cite ref="Mishnah Terumot 3:5">Ter. III, 5</cite> <he>האומר … קרא שם</he> if one says, the priest’s portion of this pile is in it …, he has named it (designated it as T’rumah).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 25:3">Gen. R. s. 25</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 5:29">Gen. V, 29</cite>) <he>לא השם הוא המדרש … הוא השם וכ׳</he> the name (<cite ref="N00468"><he>נח</he></cite>) and the interpretation (<he>ינחמנו</he>) do not correspond; it ought to be either &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 2:8">Ber. II, 8</cite> <he>ליטול … השם</he>, v. <cite ref="N00571"><he>נָטַל</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Makkot 1:2">Macc. I, 2</cite> <he>לא השם המביאו וכ׳</he> the title (the legal text) under which the false witness is doomed to lashes, is not the one under which he is bound to pay indemnity.

<cite ref="Mishnah Kinnim 1:3">Kinn. I, 3</cite> <he>משם אחד</he> sacrificial birds of the same denomination (intended for the same class of cases), opp. <he>משני שמות</he> of different denominations.

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 12:3">Sabb. XII, 3</cite> <he>משם אחד</he> two letters of the alphabet of the same name (<he>אא</he>, <cite ref="B00049"><he>בב</he></cite> &c.), opp. <he>משתי שמות</he> two different letters (<he>אב</he> &c.).

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 12:3">Ib.</cite> <he>שם קטן משם גדול וכ׳</he> a small name or word as a part (or abbreviation) of a larger one, as <cite ref="U01406"><he>שם</he></cite> as a part of <cite ref="U01517"><he>שמעון</he></cite>, of <cite ref="U01427"><he>שמואל</he></cite> &c. Ib. 103ᵇ <he>שתי אותיות והן שם אחד</he> two identical letters which represent a word, (as <cite ref="U02056"><he>שש</he></cite>, which may stand for <cite ref="U02056"><he>שֵׁשׁ</he></cite> or <cite ref="U02056"><he>שָׂשׂ</he></cite>) &c.
<cite ref="Shevuot 3b">Shebu. 3ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>לא מן השם הוא זה וכ׳</he> this comes not under this title (this is not the real reason), but it is because &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 3:4">Ker. III, 4</cite> <he>אינו מן השם</he> the offence is not of the same class.
<cite ref="Makkot 4b:7">Macc. 4ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. (<he>על חבירו</he>) <he>מוציא שם רע</he> who spreads an evil report about his neighbor (injures his reputation).

Ber. 17ᵃ גדל בשם טוב וכ׳ who has grown up with a good name, and departed life with a good name; a. v. fr.—Esp. הַשֵּׁם or שֵׁם the Divine Name, the Tetragrammaton, contradist. to כינוי attribute; in gen. the Lord.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:5">Snh. VII, 5</cite> <he>המגדף … שיפרש השם</he> the blasphemer is not punishable, unless he uses the Name explicitly.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:8">Ib. 8</cite> <he>המקלל … בַּשֵּׁם</he> he that curses his father or his mother is not punishable, unless he curses them with the Name.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 56a:19">Ib. 56ᵃ</cite> <he>בידך את השם בכינוי</he> (not <he>בכינויים</he>) if he curses God by using a divine attribute.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 56a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>עד שיברך שם בשם</he> unless he curses God and pronounces the Name.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 3:8">Yoma III, 8</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 4:2">IV, 2</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 6:2">VI, 2</cite> (<he>בשם</he>) <he>אנא השם</he> I pray, O Lord (pronouncing the Tetragrammaton).

Ib. כשהיו שומעים שם המפורש שהוא יוצא וכ׳ when they heard the Tetragrammaton pronounced &c., v. פָּרַשׁ. Ib. IV, 1 אחד … לַשֵּׁם on one of the lots was written ‘unto the Lord’; של שם the lot bearing the inscription ‘unto the Lord’; a. v. fr.; v. שָׁמַיִם.—Especial uses: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁ־ the same as, as well as.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 9:5">Ber. IX, 5</cite> <he>חייב אדם … כשם שמברך וכ׳</he> a man is bound to bless God for what is evil as well as he blesses for what is good.
<cite ref="Berakhot 62a:16">Ib. 62ᵃ</cite> <he>כשם שנפרעין וכ׳</he> as well as the dead are called to account &c., v. <cite ref="O01319"><he>סַפְדָּן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 5:1">Sot. V, 1</cite> <he>כשם שהמים … כך וכ׳</he> as the waters test her, so do they test him.
Ib. כשם שאסורה וכ׳, v. בָּעַל; a. v. fr.—בְּשֵׁם, מִשֵּׁם in the name of, in behalf of.
<cite ref="Megillah 15a:7">Meg. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>כל האומר דכר בשם אומרו וכ׳</he> he who relates a thing in the name of him who said it (gives credit to authority), brings redemption into the world.
<cite ref="Mishnah Peah 2:4">Peah II, 4</cite> <he>מִשְּׁמוֹ</he> in his own name (as his individual opinion).
Y. Taan. I, 64ᵃ הלכה … שאמר משם וכ׳ the rule follows the opinion of …, who said in behalf of &c.; a. v. fr.—לְשֵׁם for the purpose of, for the sake of, as; with reference to.

<cite ref="Gittin 24b:8">Gitt. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>כתב רחמנא לה לִשְׁמָהּ</he> the text (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 24:3">Deut. XXIV, 3</cite>) says, ‘unto her’, that means, that it must be written especially for her.
<cite ref="Yevamot 47b:7">Yeb. 47ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="U00437"><he>שׁוּם</he> II</cite>.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 99b:10">Snh. 99ᵇ</cite> <he>העוסק בתורה לשמה</he> who studies the Law for its own sake (for no selfish ends).

<cite ref="Pesachim 50b:10">Pes. 50ᵇ</cite> <he>לעולם יעסוק … אע״פ שלא לשמה … בא לשמה</he> by all means let a man engage in the study of the Law and in good deeds, even if not for their own sake, for through the work for a selfish purpose he will arrive at the stage of doing good for its own sake.

<cite ref="Pesachim 13b:4">Ib. 13ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>שחטן לִשְׁמָן וכ׳</he> if he slaughtered them as such (as festive sacrifices) &c.; <he>זרק דמן שלא לשמן</he> if he sprinkled their blood, having in mind another purpose (another class of sacrifices).

Gen. R. s. 25 לשם קרבנו נקרא he was named (נח) with reference to his sacrifice (ניחח, Gen. VIII, 21) ; לשם נחת וכ׳ he was named (נח) with reference to the rest of the ark (ותנח, Gen. VIII, 4); Yalk. ib. 42 על שם וכ׳; a. v. fr.—עַל שֵׁם (abbrev. ע״ש) with reference to, because.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:1:7">Y. Taan. II, beg. 65ᵃ</cite> <he>על שם ואנכי וכ׳</he> as a reference to (what Abraham said,) ‘and I am but dust and ashes’ (<cite ref="Genesis 18:27">Gen. XVIII, 27</cite>).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 23:7">Gen. R. s. 23</cite>, v. <cite ref="I00088"><he>טְבַרְיָא</he></cite>; a. fr.; v. <cite ref="U00437"><he>שׁוּם</he> II</cite>.—Pl. <he>שֵׁמוֹת</he>, constr. <he>שְׁמוֹת</he>. Kinn. l. c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 26:7">Gen. R. s. 26</cite> <he>כל הש׳ הללו וכ׳</he> all these names indicate rebellion &c., v. <cite ref="M02544"><he>מַרְדּוּת</he> I</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 114b:6">B. Mets. 114ᵇ</cite> <he>עובר בכל הש׳ הללו</he> is guilty under all these titles (texts).
<cite ref="Shevuot 35a:17">Shebu. 35ᵃ</cite> <he>יש ש׳ שנמחקין ויש ש׳ וכ׳</he> there are divine names which may be erased, and such as may not be erased.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:2:2">Y. R. Hash. I, 56ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>שְׁ׳ המלאכים</he>, v. <cite ref="M01470"><he>מַלְאָךְ</he></cite>; a. fr.
